TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r3.claim: The magicians' answer is rhetorically powerful, conveying profound wisdom and certainty in its wording, implications, and meaning.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r3.anchor: كلام بليغ في منطوقه بالغ في مفهومه بعيد في معناه رفيع في منزلته

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r4.claim: The magicians had been awed by Pharaoh and worldly finery, even proclaiming victory by his might; after seeing truth's signs, they lost their awe of his power and worldly status and were freed from cowardice, flattery, caprice, and longing for worldly glitter.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r4.anchor: فما لبثوا دون أن ظهرت لهم آيات الحق فبهرت أبصارهم فطاحت عند ذلك ما كانوا يرون لفرعون من عزة وسلطان

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r5.claim: The believers now attach themselves to truth and God's authority: they will what God wills, hope only in God, and fear only God.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r5.anchor: فلا يريدون إلا ما أراده الله ولا يرجون إلا الله ولا يخافون إلا الله عز اسمه

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r8.claim: The believers regard Pharaoh's worldly wealth and status as a deceptive mirage; they face a choice between truth and falsehood, and people of certainty cannot prefer the mirage over truth.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r8.anchor: فقد خيروا بين الحق، والباطل والحقيقة والسراب، وحاشا أهل اليقين أن يشكوا في يقينهم

SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r1.claim: The apparent reading takes ما as a relative pronoun in the accusative, coordinated with خطايانا: God forgives them also for what Pharaoh compelled them to do.
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r1.anchor: وفي محلها احتمالان، أحدهما: أنها منصوبة المحل نسقا على " خطايانا "

SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r2.claim: Alternatively, if ما is relative, it can be a subject with an omitted predicate: the sorcery forced on them is lifted or not held against them.
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r2.anchor: والثاني من الاحتمالين: أنها مرفوعة المحل على الابتداء والخبر محذوف تقديره:

SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa takes ما as negative and reconstructs a fronted phrase meaning their sins from sorcery are forgiven although Pharaoh did not compel them; the author says this is far from the meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r3.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " وفي الكلام تقديم، تقديره: ليغفر لنا خطايانا من/ السحر

SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r4.claim: من السحر can be a circumstantial phrase modifying the pronoun in عليه or the relative pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r4.anchor: و " من السحر " يجوز أن يكون حالا من الهاء في " عليه " أو من الموصول.

SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:73/r5.claim: Alternatively, من السحر specifies the kind of thing meant.

ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r1.claim: ما is accusative: the sense is that God forgive their sins and Pharaoh's coercion of them into sorcery.
ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r1.anchor: نصب، المعنى لتغفر لنا خطايانا وإكراهك إيانا على السحر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r2.speaker: الراوي
ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r2.claim: A report says Pharaoh had forced the sorcerers to learn sorcery.
ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r2.anchor: ويروى أن فرعون أكرههم على تعلم السحر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r3.claim: God is better and more enduring for them than Pharaoh; their words answer his threat that they would learn whose punishment was harsher and more lasting (20:71).
ZAJJAJ:v3p369/r3.anchor: أي الله خير لنا منك وأبقى عذابا لأنهم قالوا هذا له جواب قوله:

ASAD-NOTES:20:72/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:72/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:72/r2.claim: They profess faith and seek forgiveness for their faults and the magic Pharaoh had forced them to practice, trusting in God's superior and abiding goodness.
ASAD-NOTES:20:72/r2.anchor: we have come to believe in our Sustainer, [hoping] that He may forgive us our faults

ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n56/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n56/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n56/r1.claim: Pharaoh, the title of Egypt's indigenous rulers, was a god-king and embodiment of Egyptian religion, where magic was central; subjects were expected to accept it as part of life.
ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n56/r1.anchor: Pharaoh (a title borne by every indigenous ruler of Egypt) was considered to be a "god-king" and, thus, the embodiment of the Egyptian religion

ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n57/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n57/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n57/r1.claim: The phrase literally means “the most abiding,” that is, eternal; Asad refers to 55:26-27.
ASAD-NOTES:20:72#n57/r1.anchor: Lit., "and the most abiding", i.e., eternal

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r1.claim: They believe so God will forgive their disbelief and sins in the afterlife, not to gain worldly reward and thus fear Pharaoh’s threat less.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r1.anchor: التي اقترفناها من الكفر والمعاصي ولا يؤاخذنا بها في الدار الآخرة لا ليمتعنا بتلك الحياة الفانية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r2.claim: The phrase is coordinated with ‘our sins’ and means the magic they performed against Moses under Pharaoh’s coercion after he summoned them from distant cities.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r2.anchor: عطف على ( خطايانا ) أي ويغفر لنا السحر الذي عملناه في معارضة موسى عليه السلام باكراهك وحشرك ايانا من المدائن القاصية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r3.claim: They single out the magic despite its inclusion among their sins to stress their repulsion from it and their desire for forgiveness; mentioning coercion also excuses them and seeks mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r3.anchor: خصوة بالذكر مع اندراجه في خطاياهم اظاهرا لغاية نفرتهم عنه رغبتهم في مغفرته وذكر الاكراه للايذان بأنه مما يجب أن يفرد بالاستغفار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r4.claim: One account says the magicians’ leaders numbered seventy-two, two Copts and the rest Israelites, whom Pharaoh forced to learn magic.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : أن رؤساءهم كانوا اثنين وسبعين اثنان منهم من القبط والباقي من قوم اسرائيل وكان فرعون اكرههم على تعلم السحر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Pharaoh took forty Israelite boys and ordered them taught magic so no one on earth could defeat them; they were among those who later believed in Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس قال : أخذ فرعون أربعين غلاما من بني اسرائيل فأمر أن يتعلموا السحر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Pharaoh used to seize people’s children and force them to learn magic.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن كان ياخذ ولدان الناس ويجبرهم على تعلم السحر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r7.claim: Another account says Pharaoh compelled them to challenge Moses after they asked to see him asleep; his staff guarding him convinced them a sleeper’s magic would fail, but Pharaoh still made them compete.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : إنه أكرههم على المعارضة حيث روى أنهم قالوا لنا : أرنا موسى نائما ففعل فوجدوه تحرسه عصاه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r8.claim: Their earlier boasts do not contradict this admission of coercion: the boast by Pharaoh’s might could have preceded it or been bravado, as could their request for a reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r8.anchor: ولا ينافي قولهم : ( بعزة فرعون إنا لنحن الغالبون ) لاحتمال أن يكون قبل ذلك أو تجلدا كما أن قولهم : ( إن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين ) قبله كما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r9.speaker: أبو عبيد وساداتنا الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r9.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and the Ḥanafī authorities treat a ruler’s bare command as coercion even without an explicit threat, since disobedience carries expected harm, especially under a tyrant.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r9.anchor: وزعم أبو عبيد أن مجرد أمر السلطان سخصا اكراه وإن لم يتوعده والى ذلك ذهب ساداتنا الحنفيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r10.claim: God is better in Himself and more enduring in recompense, whether reward or punishment; alternatively, He is better in reward and more enduring in punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p233#2/r10.anchor: ( والله خير ( في حد ذاته تعالى ﴿ وأبقى ﴾ ) ) أي وأدوم جزاء ثوابا كان أو عقابا أو خير ثوابا وأبقى عذابا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r1.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains that Pharaoh earlier compelled people to learn magic lest the practice disappear, though the sorcerers came voluntarily now.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r1.anchor: قيل: روي عن الحسن أنه قال: كان فرعون يكره قوما على تعلم السحر لكيلا يذهب أصله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r2.claim: Muqātil says 72 sorcerers included two Copts and 70 Israelites whom Pharaoh forced to learn magic.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كانت السحرة اثنين وسبعين، اثنان من القبط وسبعون من بني إسرائيل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r3.speaker: عبد العزيز بن أبان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abān says sorcerers saw Moses' staff guard him in sleep and knew he was no sorcerer, but Pharaoh still forced them to learn magic.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285/r3.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن أبان: قالت السحرة لفرعون: أرنا موسى إذا نام، فأراهم موسى نائما وعصاه تحرسه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285#2/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says God is better in reward and more lasting in punishment than Pharaoh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285#2/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: خير منك ثوابا، وأبقى عقابا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285#2/r2.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says God gives better reward if obeyed and more lasting punishment if disobeyed, answering Pharaoh's boast.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p285#2/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: خير منك ثوابا (2) إن أطيع، وأبقى منك عذابا إن عصي

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r1.claim: Their past sins include disbelief and other acts of disobedience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r1.anchor: من الكفر والمعاصي. { وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر } من معارضة المعجزة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r2.claim: What Pharaoh forced them to do was oppose the miracle with magic.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r2.anchor: من معارضة المعجزة. روي أنهم قالوا لفرعون أرنا موسى نائما

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r3.claim: The sorcerers asked Pharaoh to show them Moses asleep; seeing his staff guard him, they judged it was not magic since a magician's power fails in sleep, but Pharaoh insisted they challenge him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r3.anchor: روي أنهم قالوا لفرعون أرنا موسى نائما فوجدوه تحرسه العصا فقالوا ما هذا بسحر

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r4.claim: The phrase can mean God is better and more lasting in reward, or better in reward and more lasting in punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:73/r4.anchor: جزاء أو خير ثوابا وأبقى عقابا.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r6.claim: They trust their Lord, who cared for them throughout their lives despite their disbelief, and seek forgiveness without implying that their faith benefits or harms God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r6.anchor: المحسن إلينا طول أعمارنا مع إساءتنا بالكفر وغيره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r7.speaker: السحرة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r7.claim: They single out the magic they were compelled to perform to counter the miracle; resisting Pharaoh would have been more fitting because God deserves greater reverence.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r7.anchor: لتعارض به المعجزة , فإن كان الأكمل لنا عصيانك فيه لأن الله أحق بأن يتقى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r8.speaker: رُوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r8.claim: One report says that only two of Pharaoh's sorcerers were Copts; the rest were Israelites whom Pharaoh forced to learn magic.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r8.anchor: روي أم الذي كان من القبط من السحرة اثنان فقط , والباقون من بني إسرائيل أكرههم فرعون على تعلم السحر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r9.speaker: رُوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r9.claim: Another report says the sorcerers saw Moses asleep while his staff guarded him and told Pharaoh that a sleeping magician's magic would fail; Pharaoh rejected this and forced them to compete.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r9.anchor: روي أنهم رأوا موسى عليه السلام نائما وعصاه تحرسه فقالوا لفرعون إن الساحر إذا نام بطل سحره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r10.claim: God is better than Pharaoh in the reward He promises and more enduring in both reward and punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r10.anchor: خير } جزاء منك فيما وعدتنا به { وأبقى * } ثوابا وعقابا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan says the apparent outcome is that God saved the sorcerers from Pharaoh; the author supports this with Qur'an 28:35 and says the end of al-Hadid is explicit about their rescue.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p31/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن الله تعالى سلمهم من فرعون , ويؤيده قوله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v5p587/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p587/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p587/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh took forty Israelite boys and ordered them taught magic so thoroughly that no one on earth could defeat them; these were the magicians who professed faith.
DURR-FULL:v5p587/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر} قال: أخذ فرعون أربعين غلاما من بني إسرائيل فأمر أن يعلموا السحر

DURR-FULL:v5p587/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p587/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v5p587/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says God is better than Pharaoh to obey, and God's punishment for disobedience lasts longer than Pharaoh himself.
DURR-FULL:v5p587/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي في قوله: {والله خير وأبقى} قال: خير منك أن أطيع وأبقى منك عذابا إن عصي

BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r1.claim: They believe in their Lord so He will forgive disbelief and other sins and spare them punishment in the afterlife, rather than extend their fleeting worldly lives in safety from Pharaoh.
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r1.anchor: من الكفر والمعاصي ولا يؤاخذ بها في الدار الآخرة لا ليمتعنا بتلك الحياة الفانية حتى تتأثر بما أوعدتنا به

BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r2.claim: Maghfira is protecting a servant from deserved punishment by overlooking sins; the root image is covering something to shield it from impurity.
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r2.anchor: والمغفرة صيانة العبد عما استحقه من العقاب للتجاوز عن ذنوبه من الغفر وهو إلباس الشيء ما يصونه عن الدنس

BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r3.claim: They include the magic they performed against Moses under Pharaoh’s coercion and after he summoned them from distant cities among the sins for which they seek forgiveness.
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r3.anchor: عطف على خطايانا أي : ويغفر لنا السحر الذي عملناه في معارضة موسى بإكراهك وحشرك إيانا من المدائن القاصية

BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r4.claim: They single out the magic although it is already included among their sins to show how thoroughly they now reject it and seek its forgiveness.
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r4.anchor: خصوه بالذكر مع اندراجه في خطاياهم إظهارا لغاية نفرتهم منه ورغبتهم في مغفرته

BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r5.claim: God is better in Himself, linking this claim to their earlier mention of the One who created them.
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r5.anchor: أي : في ذاته وهو ناظر إلى قولهم والذي فطرنا

BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r6.claim: God’s recompense lasts longer: His reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience outlast whatever Pharaoh can give or inflict.
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r6.anchor: أي : جزاء ثوابا كان أو عقابا أو خير لنا منك ثوابا إن أطعناه وأدوم عذابا منك إن عصيناه

BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r7.claim: The inward reading says God is better at bringing good and repelling harm, and His good and punishment both endure longer than Pharaoh’s.
BURSEVI:v5p312#2/r7.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {والله خير} في إيصال الخير ودفع الشر منك {وأبقى} خيره من خيرك وعذابه من عذابك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r1.claim: The sentence إنا آمنا بربنا functions as the reason for what the magicians have just said.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r1.anchor: وجملة { إنا آمنا بربنا } في محل العلة لما تضمنه كلامهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r2.claim: Pharaoh had forced them to challenge Moses with magic; they now recognize that using it to disprove God’s divinity was false and sinful, so they ask forgiveness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r2.anchor: ومعنى { وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر } أنه أكرههم على تحديهم موسى بسحرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r3.claim: The sentence والله خير وأبقى can be circumstantial or an inserted concluding statement that summarizes the preceding speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r3.anchor: وجملة { والله خير وأبقى } في موضع الحال ، أو معترضة في آخر الكلام للتذييل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r4.claim: God is better for them to prefer over Pharaoh; God’s reward and punishment last longer than Pharaoh’s, so his threat cannot terrify them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p267/r4.anchor: والمعنى : أن الله خير لنا بأن نؤثره منك ، والمراد : رضى الله ، وهو أبقى منك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r9.claim: One group says Pharaoh forced them to oppose Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r9.anchor: قالت فرقة أرادوا ما ضمهم إليه من معارضة موسى وحملهم عليه من ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r10.claim: Another says Pharaoh had long taken people's children, trained them in magic, and forced them to practice it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r10.anchor: وقالت فرقة بل كان فرعون قديما يأخذ ولدان الناس بتعليم السحر ويجبرهم على ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r11.claim: “God is better and more enduring” answers Pharaoh's question about which punishment is harsher and longer-lasting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53/r11.anchor: وقولهم خير وأبقى رد على قوله أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r1.claim: Their sins for which they seek forgiveness are their former association of partners with God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ليغفر لنا يعنون الشرك وما أكرهتنا عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r2.claim: They ask forgiveness for the magic Pharaoh coerced them into practicing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r2.anchor: أي والذي أكرهتنا عليه أي ويغفر لنا إكراهك إيانا على السحر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, as relayed by Ibn al-Anbari, explains that Pharaoh forced subjects to teach their children magic, beginning with coerced learning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس قال ابن الأنباري كان يطالب بعض أهل مملكته بأن يعلموا أولادهم السحر وهم لذلك كارهون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r4.claim: The second answer is that after seeing Moses invoke God and follow the pious path, the sorcerers feared exposing their craft, but Pharaoh insisted they challenge him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r4.anchor: والثاني أن السحرة لما شاهدوا موسى بعد قولهم أئن لنا لأجرا ورأوا ذكره الله تعالى وسلوكه منهاج المتقين جزعوا من ملاقاته بالسحر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r5.claim: The third answer is that Pharaoh compelled them to perform magic because losing before the assembled crowd would damage their standing with kings and the market.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r5.anchor: والثالث أنهم خافوا أن يغلبوا في ذلك الجمع فيقدح ذلك في صنعتهم عند الملوك والسوق وأكرههم فرعون على فعل السحر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari's fourth explanation is that Pharaoh forced them from their homelands because of the magic.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r6.anchor: والرابع أن فرعون أكرههم على مفارقة أوطانهم وكان سبب ذلك السحر ذكره هذه الأقوال ابن الأنباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r7.claim: God is better than Pharaoh in reward for obedience and more enduring in punishment for disobedience; this answers Pharaoh's threat of harsher, longer punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p308/r7.anchor: أي خير منك ثوابا إذا أطبع وأبقى عقابا إذا عصي وهذا جواب قوله ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r1.claim: The magicians ask forgiveness for their sins, especially performing magic under Pharaoh's coercion to counter God's sign and His prophet's miracle.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r1.anchor: أي: ما كان منا من الآثام، خصوصا ما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh took forty Israelite youths and ordered them trained in magic at al-Farama; they became among the magicians who believed in Moses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر} قال: أخذ فرعون أربعين غلاما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r3.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam gives the same account about the Israelite youths trained by Pharaoh.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r3.anchor: وكذا قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq's interpretation is that God is better for the magicians than Pharaoh, and God's reward lasts longer than Pharaoh's promise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r4.anchor: وهو رواية عن ابن إسحاق، رحمه الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi explains that God is better if obeyed and more enduring in punishment if disobeyed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: {والله خير} أي: لنا منك إن أطيع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir says a similar explanation is also narrated from Ibn Ishaq.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r6.anchor: وروي نحوه عن ابن إسحاق أيضا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره من السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and other early authorities said the magicians began the day as magicians and ended it as martyrs, supporting the report that Pharaoh carried out his threat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r7.anchor: ولهذا قال ابن عباس وغيره من السلف: أصبحوا سحرة، وأمسوا شهداء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir considers it apparent that Pharaoh resolved to execute the magicians and did so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن فرعون -لعنه الله-صمم على ذلك وفعله بهم

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r16.claim: Their خطايا are their sins and disobedient acts.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r16.anchor: إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا أي: معاصينا

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r17.claim: What Pharaoh compelled them to do was the practice and learning of magic.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r17.anchor: وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر أي: ما أمرتنا من عمل السحر وتعلمه

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r18.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh handed boys over to be taught magic.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r18.anchor: وقيل: إنه دفع غلمانا إلى السحر، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r19.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r19.claim: Muqatil says the magicians were seventy-two Israelites whom Pharaoh forced to learn magic.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r19.anchor: وقيل: كانت السحرة اثنين وسبعين من بني إسرائيل أكرههم على تعلم السحر، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r20.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r20.claim: Abu Muslim says Pharaoh’s coercion consisted of gathering them from towns and regions to perform magic against Moses.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r20.anchor: وقيل: إكراهه أنه حشرهم من المدائن والأقطار لعمل السحر ليقابل بهم موسى، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r1.claim: Some say the magicians resisted after seeing the staff’s sign, which could not be magic, and Pharaoh then forced them.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنهم امتنعوا لما علموا من حديث العصا، وأن مثله لا يكون سحرا فأكرههم

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r2.claim: Another explanation is that kings traditionally forced elders to teach magic to young people so the practice would not die out.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r2.anchor: وقيل: كانت عادة الملوك أن يكرهوا الكبار على تعليم الشبان السحر كيلا يتعطل

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r3.speaker: عبد العزيز بن أبان
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r3.claim: The magicians asked Pharaoh to show them Moses asleep; seeing his staff guard him, they concluded his power was not magic, since a magician’s magic ceases during sleep, but Pharaoh still made them work.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r3.anchor: قالوا لفرعون: أرنا موسى إذا نام، فأراهم، فإذا هو نائم وعصاه تحرسه، فقالوا: ليس هذا بسحر

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r4.claim: God gives believers better and more enduring reward, and disobedient people more enduring punishment than Pharaoh can, since Pharaoh will perish.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r4.anchor: قيل: خير ثوابا وأبقى للمؤمنين، وأبقى عقابا للعاصين منك؛ لأنك فان هالك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.claim: The three preceding verses are either a quotation of the magicians' speech or God's account rather than a quotation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.anchor: قيل في هذه الآيات الثلاث : هي حكاية قولهم . وقيل : خبر من الله لا على وجه الحكاية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r6.claim: God is better than Pharaoh and more enduring in reward if obeyed and punishment if disobeyed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r6.anchor: والله خير منك وأبقى ثوابا إن أطيع , وعقابا إن عصي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r7.claim: Alternatively, God is better than Pharaoh in reward if obeyed and more enduring than him in punishment if disobeyed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p414/r7.anchor: خير منك ثوابا إن أطيع وأبقى منك عقابا إن عصي

MUQATIL:20:72-73/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:72-73/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:72-73/r2.claim: Their faith means affirming God's oneness.

MUQATIL:20:72-73/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:72-73/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:72-73/r3.claim: Their errors were their magic, including what Pharaoh forced them to perform; God is better and more enduring than Pharaoh, who dies while God alone remains, answering Pharaoh's claim in 20:71.
MUQATIL:20:72-73/r3.anchor: يعنى ما جبرتناعليه { من السحر والله خير وأبقى }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r1.claim: Mā is a relative pronoun, the object coordinated with our sins; min al-siḥr is a circumstantial phrase modifying it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r1.anchor: ﴿ إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا وما أكرهتنا عليه ﴾ ما موصولة منصوبة بالعطف على خطايانا ﴿ من السحر ﴾ حال من ما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r2.claim: A report says the sorcerers saw Moses guarded by his staff while asleep, recognized that this was no ordinary magic, and feared exposure; Pharaoh compelled them to perform magic, harming himself through ignorance while their knowledge benefited them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r2.anchor: روى أنهم قالوا لفرعون أرنا موسى نائما ففعل فوجدوه وتحرسه عصاه فقالوا ما هذا بسحر الساحر إذا نام بطل سحره

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r3.claim: God gives the better reward to the obedient and the more lasting punishment to the disobedient, rebutting Pharaoh's threat in 20:71.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62/r3.anchor: ﴿ والله خير ﴾ ثوابا لمن أطاعه ﴿ وأبقى ﴾ عقاب المن عصاه وهو رد لقول فرعون ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r16.claim: ما may be accusative, coordinated with خطايانا.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r16.anchor: «ما» في موضع نصب معطوفة على الخطايا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r17.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r17.claim: Alternatively ما has no syntactic position and negates: forgive our sins apart from the magic forced on us.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r17.anchor: وقيل: لا موضع لها وهي نافية أي ليغفر لنا خطايانا من السحر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r18.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r18.claim: Al-Naḥḥās prefers the first, accusative analysis.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r18.anchor: وما أكرهتنا عليه. النحاس: والأول أولى.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r19.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r19.claim: Al-Mahdawī finds the negation view strained because the magicians had asked whether they would receive a reward if victorious at 26:41.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:72-73/r19.anchor: النحاس: والأول أولى. المهدوي: وفيه بعد لقولهم:

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r1.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r1.claim: Al-Mahdawī adds that coercion is not a sin, though they may have been compelled to learn magic as children.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r1.anchor: ولأن الإكراه ليس بذنب، وإن كان يجوز أن يكونوا أكرهوا على تعليمه صغارا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they learned magic as children but later practiced it voluntarily.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: كانوا يعلمون السحر أطفالا ثم عملوه مختارين بعد

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r3.claim: ما can be nominative as subject with an omitted predicate: the magic Pharaoh forced on them is set aside from them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون «ما» في موضع رفع بالابتداء ويضمر الخبر،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r4.claim: من السحر attaches to أكرهتنا under the first two analyses, but to خطايانا under the negation analysis.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r4.anchor: و«من السحر» على هذا القول والقول الأول يتعلق ب«أكرهتنا». وعلى أن «ما» نافية يتعلق ب«خطايانا».

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the omitted noun to be God's reward: His reward is better and more enduring.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r5.anchor: أي ثوابه خير وأبقى فحذف المضاف قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r6.claim: Another view says God is better for them than Pharaoh, and His punishment lasts longer than Pharaoh's.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r6.anchor: وقيل: الله خير لنا منك وأبقى عذابا لنا من عذابك لنا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r7.claim: Another view means God is better if obeyed and more enduring in punishment if disobeyed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r7.anchor: وقيل: الله خير لنا إن أطعناه، وأبقى عذابا منك إن عصيناه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r8.claim: The statement answers Pharaoh's threat at 20:71.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r8.anchor:
وهو جواب قوله:
ولتعلمن أينآ أشد عذابا وأبقى

QASHANI:20:72-73/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:72-73/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:72-73/r3.claim: Forgiveness means covering with divine light the dark forms and blameworthy traits produced by attachment to natural pleasures and worldly adornments.
QASHANI:20:72-73/r3.anchor: يستر بنوره الهيئات المظلمة والصفات الرديئة التي عرضت لنفوسنا بسبب الميل إلى اللذات الطبيعية

QASHANI:20:72-73/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:72-73/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:72-73/r4.claim: The magicians had recognized Moses' truth by their innate preparedness and tried to decline competing with him, but Pharaoh compelled them to perform magic.
QASHANI:20:72-73/r4.anchor: بنور استعدادهم وعلموا كونه على الحق

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r8.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r8.claim: Al-Qadi calls Ikrima's report remote: seeing Paradise directly would compel belief and undermine the voluntary faith expressed in their plea for forgiveness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r8.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا بعيد لأنه تعالى لو أراهم عيانا لصاروا ملجئين

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r9.claim: Razi replies that Abraham, despite certainty of forgiveness, still said he hoped God would forgive him; the magicians could similarly speak of hope after a vision.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r9.anchor: لما جاز لإبراهيم عليه السلام مع قطعه بكونه مغفورا له أن يقول

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says rulers compelled some subjects to learn magic, then required older practitioners to teach youths, so the magicians were forced both to learn and teach.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r8.anchor: أولا والتعليم ثانيا مكرهين قاله ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r9.claim: Another account says there were seventy-two leading magicians, two Copts and the rest Israelites; they saw Moses' staff guard him while he slept and concluded he was no magician, yet Pharaoh insisted on a contest.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r9.anchor: أن رؤساء السحرة كانوا اثنين وسبعين ، إثنان من القبط ، والباقي من بني إسرائيل

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r10.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says magicians were forcibly assembled from the cities to challenge Moses and perhaps compelled to perform magic as well.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r10.anchor: قال الحسن : إن السحرة حشروا من المدائن ليعارضوا موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r11.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r11.claim: Amr ibn Ubayd says a ruler's summons is coercion; Razi rejects this because a summons without fear is not compulsion.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r11.anchor: قال عمرو بن عبيد : دعوة السلطان إكراه وهذا ضعيف لأن دعوة السلطان

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r12.claim: God is better in reward for obedience and more enduring in punishment for disobedience, answering Pharaoh's claim about which side has harsher, longer punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r12.anchor: ثوابا لمن أطاعه . { وأبقى } عقابا لمن عصاه

RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r14.claim: Their speech turns from the threat and their steadfast response to the contrasting fates of believers and criminals at the Resurrection, beginning with the criminal's Hell in 20:74.
RAZI-FULL:v22p77/r14.anchor: ثم ختموا هذا الكلام بشرح أحوال المؤمنين وأحوال المجرمين في عرصة القيامة

TAB-FULL:v16p117/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r1.claim: They professed their Lord's oneness, believed His promise and threat, and ask Him to forgive and conceal their sins.
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r1.anchor: تعلمناه من السحر، وعملنا به الذي أكرهتنا على تعلمه والعمل به

TAB-FULL:v16p117/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r2.claim: They ask forgiveness for magic learned and practiced under Pharaoh's compulsion, since he compelled them to learn it.
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r2.anchor: تعلمناه من السحر، وعملنا به الذي أكرهتنا على تعلمه والعمل به

TAB-FULL:v16p117/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh gave boys to sorcerers to teach them magic at al-Faramā.
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، في قول الله تبارك وتعالى: {وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر} [طه: 73] قال: غلمان دفعهم فرعون إلى السحرة

TAB-FULL:v16p117/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says Pharaoh ordered them to learn magic; they left God's Book and instructed their people to teach it.
TAB-FULL:v16p117/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر} [طه: 73] قال: أمرهم بتعلم السحر، قال: تركوا كتاب الله

TAB-FULL:v16p119/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p119/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p119/r1.claim: God is better than Pharaoh as rewarder of the obedient, and more lasting in punishment for those who disobey and oppose Him.
TAB-FULL:v16p119/r1.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، {والله خير وأبقى} [طه: 73] خير منك ثوابا، وأبقى عذابا

TAB-FULL:v16p119/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p119/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p119/r2.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says God is better than Pharaoh in reward and more lasting in punishment.
TAB-FULL:v16p119/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، {والله خير وأبقى} [طه: 73] خير منك ثوابا، وأبقى عذابا

TAB-FULL:v16p119/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p119/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب ومحمد بن قيس
TAB-FULL:v16p119/r3.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb and Muḥammad ibn Qays say God is better than Pharaoh if obeyed and more lasting in punishment if disobeyed.
TAB-FULL:v16p119/r3.anchor: عن أبي معشر، عن محمد بن كعب، ومحمد بن قيس، في قول الله: {والله خير وأبقى} [طه: 73] قالا: خيرا منك إن أطيع

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r5.claim: Khataya is the plural of khatiʾa and is close in meaning to sayyiʾa, a misdeed.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r5.anchor: الخطايا جمع خطيئة وهي قريبة معنى من السيئة

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r6.claim: The phrase about coerced magic is coordinated with “our sins,” and min al-sihr explains what they were compelled to do.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r6.anchor: معطوف على { خطايانا } و { من السحر } بيان له والمعنى

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r7.claim: Their words show coercion, either when they were summoned from their districts to Pharaoh or when the dispute and whispering led them into the contest.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r7.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أنهم أكرهوا عليه إما حين حشروا إلى فرعون من خلال ديارهم وإما حين تنازعوا أمرهم بينهم

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r8.claim: Their request for forgiveness explains their refusal to prefer Pharaoh: they chose the God who created them and believe in Him to forgive their sins and coerced magic.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r8.anchor: أي إنما اخترنا الله الذي فطرنا عليك وآمنا به ليغفر لنا خطايانا

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r9.claim: God’s goodness and permanence explain why they prefer His forgiveness over Pharaoh’s favor; absolutely, nothing is better or more enduring than He is.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r9.anchor: أي خير من كل خير وأبقى من كل باق - لمكان الإطلاق -

TABATABAI:20:73#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r10.claim: Their closing words deliberately answer Pharaoh’s claim that he can inflict the harshest and most lasting punishment.
TABATABAI:20:73#2/r10.anchor: وفي هذا الذيل نوع مقابلة لما في ذيل كلام فرعون

TABATABAI:20:74-75/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r1.claim: Calling Him their Lord fits their confession of faith and worship, since lordship includes ownership and governance.
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r1.anchor: وأما الثاني فلأن فيه إخبارا عن الإيمان به وأمس صفاته تعالى بالإيمان والعبودية صفة ربوبيته المتضمنة لمعنى الملك والتدبير

TABATABAI:20:74-75/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r2.claim: They use the name Allah because goodness rests on perfection, and God possesses every perfection, making Him absolutely good.
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r2.anchor: لأن ملاك خيرية الشيء الكمال وعنده تعالى جميع صفات الكمال القاضية بخيريته المطلقة

TABATABAI:20:74-75/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r3.claim: Their three descriptions carry the argument: they will not prefer Pharaoh because God created them, believe in Him because He is Lord, and hold Him best because He is God.
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r3.anchor: لن نؤثرك على الذي فطرنا لأنه فطرنا، وإنا آمنا بربنا

FARRA:v2p187/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p187/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p187/r3.claim: ما is accusative and refers back to the sense of الخطايا.
FARRA:v2p187/r3.anchor: ما في موضع نصب مردودة على معنى الخطايا.

FARRA:v2p187/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p187/r4.speaker: التفسير
FARRA:v2p187/r4.claim: A tafsīr report says Pharaoh forced the magicians to learn sorcery.
FARRA:v2p187/r4.anchor: وذكر في التفسير أن فرعون كان أكره السحرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says their sins were the idolatry they had practiced.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (الشرك الذي كنا فيه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r2.claim: One report says Pharaoh forced people to learn sorcery; another says he forced them to oppose Moses with magic. Both explanations are transmitted in tafsir.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r2.anchor: روي: (أن فرعون # كان يكره الناس على تعلم السحر) (¬1). وروي: (أنه أكرههم على معارضة موسى بالسحر)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the comparison to mean that God’s reward is better and more enduring, with “reward” understood implicitly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد ثواب الله خير وأبقى)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says God is better for them than Pharaoh and more enduring in punishment, answering Pharaoh’s threat in 20:71.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (أي الله خير لنا منك وأبقى عذابا) (¬4). وهذا جواب قوله: {ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq explains that God is better than Pharaoh in reward and more enduring in punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r5.anchor: وهذا معنى قول محمد بن إسحاق: (والله خير منك [ثوابا وأبقى عقابا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says God is better than Pharaoh if obeyed, and His punishment lasts longer than Pharaoh’s if disobeyed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p466/r6.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: (والله خير منك إن أطيع، وأبقى عذابا منك] (¬6) إن عصي)

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r1.claim: God is better than what Pharaoh called them to and more enduring.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r2.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r2.claim: Some say that God is better than Pharaoh and more enduring.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: منك يا فرعون وأبقى

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r3.claim: Qatadah says the magicians began the day as sorcerers and ended it as martyrs.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r3.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: كانوا أول النهار سحرة وآخره شهداء

BURHAN:v4p228/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p228/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p228/r1.claim: The use of إن for causation is agreed upon and suits the two verses under discussion, with the sense “because He gave it” and “so that they would not believe.”
BURHAN:v4p228/r1.anchor: ورد بان استعمالها للتعليل مجمع عليه وهو لائق في هاتين الايتين والتقدير لان آتاه ولئلا يصدقوا

BURHAN:v4p228/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p228/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p228/r8.claim: The open, doubled form of إن can also emphasize, though some object that expanding it as a verbal noun seems to lose emphasis; the author calls this objection weak.
BURHAN:v4p228/r8.anchor: إن المفتوحة المشددة يجئ للتاكيد كالمكسورة واستشكله بعضهم لانك لوصرحت بالمصدر المنسبك منها لم تفد توكيدا وهو ضعيف

BURHAN:v4p228/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p228/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p228/r9.claim: Al-Mufassal distinguishes the forms: kasra إن emphasizes a complete independent sentence, while open إن turns its clause into a noun-like unit that needs another clause element.
BURHAN:v4p228/r9.anchor: وقال في المفصل إن وان تؤكدان مضمون الجملة إلا إن المكسورة الجملة معها على استقلالها بفائدتها والمفتوحة تقلبها إلى حكم المفرد

BURHAN:v4p228/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p228/r10.speaker: ابن الحاجب
BURHAN:v4p228/r10.claim: Ibn al-Hajib explains that kasra إن leaves the sentence complete while adding emphasis; open إن makes its clause noun-like, so it must join another constituent, as in “I like that Zayd is standing.”
BURHAN:v4p228/r10.anchor: قال ابن الحاجب لان وضع إن تاكيد للجملة من غير تغيير لمعناها فوجب إن تستقل بالفائدة بعد دخولها

NAHHAS:v3p49/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p49/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p49/r7.claim: The preferred analysis makes ما accusative by coordination with خطايانا.
NAHHAS:v3p49/r7.anchor: ( ما ) في موضع نصب معطوفة على الخطايا وقيل لا موضع لها

NAHHAS:v3p49/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p49/r8.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v3p49/r8.claim: An alternative treats ما as a negative particle with no syntactic position: God will forgive their sins and what Pharaoh forced them to do.
NAHHAS:v3p49/r8.anchor: وقيل لا موضع لها وهي نافية أي ليغفر لنا خطايانا من السحر وما أكرهتنا عليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r1.claim: In the lover’s line, the day of separation is black, then the heart of one who never loved is added as a witty completion because the loveless heart is imagined as still darker and callous.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r1.anchor: ولقد ذكرتك والزمان كأنه يوم النوى وفؤاد من لم يعشق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r2.claim: The common phrase night like a hypocrite’s or unbeliever’s heart has some literal grounding because a heart can be conceived as black; Ibn al-ʿAmīd’s darker than unbelief is a direct equal comparison.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r2.anchor: ليل كقلب المنافق أو الكافر إلا أن في هذا شوبا من الحقيقة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r3.claim: Jurjānī allows reading al-Buḥturī’s line about Sunna and innovation as truth growing more beautiful when falsehood is exposed, like stars against darkness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r3.anchor: وإن تأولت في قوله سنن لاح بينهن ابتداع أنه أراد معنى قولهم إن سواد الظلام يزيد النجوم حسنا وبهاء كان له مذهب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r4.claim: Even on that reading, the image still departs from the surface by giving abstract Sunna and innovation visible colors, so one can seem to brighten the other.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p198/r4.anchor: إلا أنه على ذلك لا يخرج من أن يكون خارجا عن الظاهر أن يمثل المعقول في ذلك بالمحسوس

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p299/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p299/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p299/r1.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz daringly reverses the moon’s conventional role as the standard of beauty, describing it as spotted and albino and claiming its light is weaker than the sun’s while its heat remains.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p299/r1.anchor: أول ما يقع في النفوس إذ أريد المبالغة في الوصف بالجمال والبلوغ فيه غاية الكمال فيقال وجه كأنه القمر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p299/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p299/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p299/r2.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan’s elegy turns the horror of Ibn Baqiyya’s crucifixion into honor: height becomes distinction, onlookers become a delegation at prayer, extended hands become gifts, and wind becomes a shroud.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p299/r2.anchor: ما صنع فيها من السحر حتى قلب جملة ما يستنكر من أحوال المصلوب إلى خلافها

STUDYQURAN:20:71/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r1.speaker: K
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r1.claim: The sorcerers’ certainty in God made them see worldly trials and pleasures as fleeting and finite beside eternal felicity in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r1.anchor: The sorcerers reached such a high degree of certainty in God that they came to see the trials and pleasures of this life as merely passing

STUDYQURAN:20:71/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r2.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r2.claim: God’s rewards exceed Pharaoh’s rewards, and God’s punishment, when meted out, lasts longer than Pharaoh’s punishment.
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r2.anchor: the rewards that God can give are better than the rewards that Pharaoh can give, and that God’s Punishment, when meted out, is more lasting

STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.claim: The passage is cross-referenced with 7:123–26 and, for verse 71, 26:49.
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.anchor: See commentary on 7:123–26; cf. also v. 71 with 26:49

TABRISI:20:71-74/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r19.claim: Their sins include associating others with God and other disobedience.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r19.anchor: من الشرك والمعاصي { وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر }

TABRISI:20:71-74/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r20.claim: They say kings forced magicians to teach magic so that it would not pass out of their control.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r20.anchor: لأن الملوك كانوا يجبرونهم على تعليم السحر كيلا يخرج السحر من أيديهم

TABRISI:20:71-74/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r21.speaker: عبد العزيز بن أبان
TABRISI:20:71-74/r21.claim: The magicians said Pharaoh showed them Moses asleep, with his staff guarding him; they said this was not magic because a magician’s spell ceases in sleep, but Pharaoh forced them to perform.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r21.anchor: فأبى عليهم إلا أن يعملوا فذلك إكراههم عن عبد العزيز بن أبان

TABRISI:20:71-74/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r22.claim: One explanation: God is better for them than Pharaoh, and His reward lasts longer than Pharaoh’s reward.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r22.anchor: أي والله خير لنا منك وثوابه أبقى لنا من ثوابك

TABRISI:20:71-74/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r23.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r23.claim: Alternatively, God’s reward for believers is better and His punishment for sinners more enduring than Pharaoh’s.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r23.anchor: وقيل: معناه والله خير ثوابا للمؤمنين وأبقى عقابا للعاصين منك

TABRISI:20:71-74/r24.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r24.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r24.claim: This answers Pharaoh’s challenge about which of the two would inflict the harsher and more lasting punishment.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r24.anchor: وهذا جواب لقوله { ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r9.claim: Their sins are the association with God in which they had lived.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r10.claim: They also seek forgiveness for the magic Pharaoh forced them to learn.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r11.claim: God is better than Pharaoh and more enduring, since Pharaoh will perish.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r8.claim: The believers’ reply confirms the comparison: God is better than Pharaoh, and His reward and punishment outlast Pharaoh’s favor and threat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r8.anchor: ويدل على أن ذلك مراد فرعون ما قابل به المؤمنون

ITQAN:v3p229/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p229/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p229/r4.claim: Some give this as a shift from address to first-person speech, but it fails because the intended speakers are not one referent.
ITQAN:v3p229/r4.anchor: وهذا المثال لا يصح لأن شرط الالتفات أن يكون المراد به واحدا
